message.reasoning:
Checking PED-25780: payment amount and transaction ID match exactly, received before the deadline, so it's paid. Moving to PED-12591, I need to verify the payment timing by converting the UTC timestamp to the local -03:00 offset to see if it arrived before the 19:59 expiration.

Confirming it's paid, PED-12591 arrived at 19:44, before the 19:59 cutoff. For PED-91312 I note a duplicate payment entry sharing the same e2e_id, so I count it once, and it matches the order amount and arrived before expiry, so paid. PED-53203 shows a payment amount lower than what was owed, marking it underpaid. PED-33934 and PED-26475 both have correct amounts but arrived after their expiration times by varying margins, so both are late_paid. PED-30476 has no linked payment at all, so it's unpaid. Now I'm checking PED-51837, converting its payment timestamp to local time to compare against the 15:02 expiration.

For PED-20098 I find two separate transfers of the same amount, both matching the order value individually but summing to double the order total — that makes it overpaid since more was received than owed. I verify PED-96039's duplicate transaction counts once and confirms as paid since it landed before expiry. Then I flag one payment with no matching order reference as an orphan transaction, and start compiling the list of payment IDs associated with each order for the final summary.
